name: wikipedia-ai
title: Signs of AI writing (Wikipedia)
description: Tells catalogued by Wikipedia editors reviewing AI-generated article text.

rules.name: AI vocabulary words
rules.description: Words LLMs lean on far more than people do: “delve”, “tapestry”, “meticulous”, “pivotal”, “intricate”, “interplay”, “underscore”, “garner”, “bolster”, “vibrant”, “bustling”, “multifaceted”, “seamless”, “ever-evolving”. One hit can be coincidence — several is a tell.
rules.suggest: Swap for a plainer word. One hit is coincidence; several is a tell.

hit: We delve into the intricacies of the interplay.
Her vibrant tapestry hung in the bustling hall.
A meticulously curated, seamless experience.
miss: The report was thorough and well organized.

rules.name: “Not just X, but Y”
rules.description: Negative parallelisms: “not just X, but (also) Y”, “not only … but …”, and the “it’s not X — it’s Y” contrast.
rules.suggest: Pick the accurate half. Negative parallelism inflates without adding.

hit: This is not just a tool, but a philosophy.
It was not merely mistaken, but dangerous.
Not only fast but also reliable.
It’s not a bug — it’s a feature.
miss: She was not sure about the plan.
not only because performance differences impair the system, but the effect is small

rules.note: Tightened from upstream, which also matched "not only" negating a clause rather than a thing. Over 18 matched document pairs this cut hits on human prose from 5 to 3 while keeping all 3 on AI prose. See research/audit.md.

rules.name: “It’s important to note”
rules.description: Didactic hedging: “it is important to note that”, “it’s worth noting”, “it should be noted”, plus the “worth pausing / considering / asking” family.
rules.suggest: Delete the hedge and state the fact.

hit: It is important to note that timing matters.
It’s worth noting the fees are separate.
It should be noted that this changed in 2020.
It's worth pausing on that number.
It is worth asking who benefits.

rules.name: “Stands as a testament”
rules.description: “Stands / serves as a testament (or reminder)”, “is a testament to” — inflating significance instead of saying what happened.
rules.suggest: Say what happened instead of what it supposedly proves.

hit: The building stands as a testament to postwar optimism.
Her career is a testament to persistence.
It serves as a stark reminder that nothing lasts.
miss: He read from the Old Testament.

rules.name: “Plays a crucial role”
rules.description: “Plays a crucial / pivotal / vital / key / significant role in …”.

hit: Volunteers play a crucial role in the program.
She played a truly pivotal role in the merger.
miss: He plays the role of the villain.

rules.name: “Ever-evolving landscape”
rules.description: Scene-setting boilerplate: “the ever-evolving / changing / shifting landscape”, “in today’s fast-paced world”.
rules.suggest: Cut the scene-setting and start with the subject.

hit: Adapting to an ever-evolving landscape.
The rapidly changing landscape of retail.
In today’s fast-paced world, attention is scarce.
miss: The landscape outside the window was gray.

rules.name: “Experts argue”
rules.description: Vague attribution to unnamed authorities: “experts argue”, “some critics have noted”, “observers suggest”, “industry reports indicate”.
rules.suggest: Name the source, or drop the claim.

hit: Experts argue that the policy failed.
Some critics have noted a decline in quality.
Industry reports suggest strong demand.
miss: Dr. Chen argued the opposite in her paper.

rules.name: “Despite these challenges”
rules.description: The boilerplate challenges-and-outlook formula: “despite these challenges”, “faces several challenges”, “challenges remain”, “remains to be seen”, “time will tell”.
rules.suggest: Replace the formula with the specific challenge and outcome.

hit: Despite these challenges, growth continued.
The sector faces several challenges.
Whether it works remains to be seen.
Only time will tell whether it sticks.
Time will tell.
miss: He arrived on time and will tell you himself.

rules.name: Participle sentence tails
rules.description: Superficial analysis bolted onto a sentence end: “…, highlighting / underscoring / showcasing / reflecting the …”.
rules.suggest: End the sentence. The participle tail adds commentary, not information.

hit: The bridge reopened in June, highlighting the city’s investment in infrastructure.
Sales doubled, underscoring the strength of the brand.
miss: She kept highlighting passages in yellow.
The team, reflecting on the loss, regrouped.

rules.name: Promotional boilerplate
rules.description: Travel-brochure tone: “nestled in”, “in the heart of”, “rich tapestry / heritage”, “hidden gem”, “boasts a”, “breathtaking”, “stunning views”.
rules.suggest: Drop the brochure register and describe plainly.

hit: The inn is nestled in a quiet valley.
The museum boasts a rich tapestry of exhibits.
Located in the heart of downtown.
A hidden gem with breathtaking views.
miss: The soup was rich and hearty.

rules.name: Chatbot leftovers
rules.description: Artifacts pasted straight from a chatbot: “as an AI language model”, “as of my last update”, “knowledge cutoff”, plus markup debris like “oaicite”, “contentReference”, “turn0search” and “utm_source=” tracking parameters.
rules.suggest: Remove the artifact. This is chatbot output pasted verbatim.

hit: As of my last update, the API was in beta.
As an AI language model, I cannot form opinions.
See example.com/page?utm_source=chatgpt.com for details.
contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}
miss: The last update shipped on Tuesday.
